finding: There is no live range for this job on the site today (live is null), so this is a first build, not a check. Built totals (parts + stated hours x $120-$160/hr, the national middle labor rate used for these checks): economy 2015 Corolla about $40-$111 (0.17-0.5 hr); midsize 2016 CR-V about $42-$110 (0.17-0.5 hr); truck 2016 F-150 about $42-$111 (0.17-0.5 hr); luxury 2015 BMW 328i about $57-$202 (0.3-1.0 hr). Posted menu prices for the filter alone run $24.99 to $78.88 at four sellers, which sits inside the mainstream built range; three of the four are $25-$31, close to the price of the filter itself, so many shops charge little or nothing for the labor. A supportable range for the site is roughly $25-$110 for mainstream vehicles and up to about $200 for European cars where the airbox is harder to reach. RepairPal ($67-$84 for one compact car) and Jerry ($73-$142) sit in the upper half of that; YourMechanic's $166 and up is a mobile visit charge and is not comparable to a shop adding the filter to other work. How solid the numbers are: the parts prices are firm for the genuine filter (list price $30-$42 on all four examples), but the low ends for the Corolla, CR-V and F-150 are discounted genuine parts, because no aftermarket price with confirmed fitment could be loaded; aftermarket filters are usually cheaper still (CR-V filters of unconfirmed year were $16-$25). The BMW part number is not confirmed for the 2015 328i sedan on the maker catalog page, and a second, dearer filter ($27-$39 aftermarket) is also listed for the 328i. The labor times are the weak part: no manufacturer, bulletin or trade-press source states a time for this job, so every class rests on one consumer guide's general figures (10-30 minutes; 0.7-1.0 hr for some European or turbo cars), with a how-to that says as little as 5 minutes. None is for the example vehicle. Menu prices came from 6 sellers (5 dealers, 1 independent) in 6 states; two of them bundle the cabin filter and are marked as a different service; no national chain prints a price for this service on the pages loaded. Held (2026-11-20, first attempt): every labor figure comes from another estimator's consumer guide, which may be used only as a comparison, and no maker, trade-press or parts-seller time for one engine air filter was found. Three of four low parts prices are a discounted genuine filter.
extras: This is usually sold alongside an oil change or a mileage service, not as its own visit, and it is often offered together with a cabin air filter (posted prices for both filters together: $137.99 to $169.95). A quote may add shop supplies and sales tax. Performance or washable filters cost far more than a standard paper element ($57-$114 on the listings seen). On a few engines the filter housing is harder to reach and the labor is higher.
